label: SENSE_COGNITION_2, contrast to intellect: In ST I q.14 a.1, sense is cognitive because it receives…
definition: In ST I q.14 a.1, sense is cognitive because it receives species without matter; intellect is more cognitive because more separate and unmixed with matter. Sense cognition is not by itself intellectual cognition.
note: This contrast uses the source article’s hierarchy of cognition, not a new formal psychology. HasIntellect remains primitive and is not identified with every kind of cognition.
